sections.title: Catch forged documents *in seconds*
body: The engine at **upokari.ai** checks the documents people are most often cheated with: land records, TCB cards and National IDs. It catches counterfeit cards, photos of screens, photocopies and edited genuine originals, then checks the details against the issuing record. No paperwork and no office visit.
Each check ends with a clear verdict: **Genuine**, **Counterfeit**, **Replay** (a photo of a screen), **Copy** or **Spoof**.

sections.title: What it checks
rows: Nokol, Khatian, Dag and plot sheets, CS–RS records, mutation and deed copies. Each is sealed, then checked page by page.
Counterfeit, cloned and altered TCB beneficiary cards, caught before any goods are handed over.
Smart NID cards and printed NID copies: layout, background pattern, MRZ checksum and the holder’s photo.
Chip data, MRZ lines, laminate and holograms, compared with the sealed issuing record.
Driving and trade licences, birth and death certificates, land-related approvals and other smart-card credentials.

items.title: Counterfeit cards
items.text: Fonts, layout, fine patterns, microprint, hologram and MRZ checksum compared with the genuine template.

items.title: Photos of screens
items.text: Spots cards captured from a phone or monitor screen by the tell-tale patterns and glare they leave.

items.title: Photocopies and scans
items.text: Finds the toner dots, soft edges and lost detail that give away a copy.

items.title: Edited genuine cards
items.text: Catches a real card with a swapped photo, laid-over details or a laminated edit.

items.title: Holograms
items.text: Checks holograms and colour-shifting features across angles.

items.title: Registry check
items.text: Matches the card number, holder details and seal with the issuing registry before giving a verdict.

sections.title: How land records are sealed: seven steps
sections.lead: From fragile registry paper to a certified copy that anyone can check.

items.title: Archival scan
items.text: Registry paper is scanned at 300 to 600 DPI on scanners suited to bound or fragile records.

items.title: Reading the fields
items.text: Software tuned for Bangla and English reads the Mouza, Khatian and Dag numbers, owner names, land area and dates.

items.title: Officer review
items.text: A registry officer checks the reading side by side with the scan. Nothing is approved automatically.

items.title: Sealing
items.text: Each page gets a digital fingerprint (SHA-256), chained page to page into one fingerprint for the whole document.

items.title: Watermark and QR
items.text: A watermark and a QR code on every page carry the document ID, page number and page fingerprint.

items.title: Stamp and copy code
items.text: A unique ID and an anti-copy micro-pattern are printed over the official stamp on the last page.

items.title: Issue and verify
items.text: The certified Nokol is printed from the sealed master. Anyone can scan it or upload a photo for a Genuine, Tampered or Copy verdict.

sections.title: Built so no one can quietly change a record

items.title: Page-by-page fingerprints:
items.text: every page’s SHA-256 fingerprint is chained to the next, so changing one page breaks the chain.

items.title: Anchored on a private blockchain:
items.text: document fingerprints are recorded on Hyperledger Fabric, so even a database administrator cannot alter them unnoticed. [What is a blockchain?](service:blockchain-technology)

items.title: Keys in secure hardware:
items.text: the signing keys are sealed in a FIPS 140-3 hardware security module.

items.title: People stay in charge:
items.text: a registry officer approves every reading before a record is sealed.

items.q: Is upokari.ai the same as the Upokari app?
items.a: They are part of the same family but do different jobs. upokari.ai is the verification engine that checks whether a document is genuine. The Upokari app is a secure mailbox and document vault on your phone. Upokari eCom is an online marketplace with its own seller app.

items.q: Which documents can the Verification Engine check?
items.a: Land documents (Nokol, Khatian, Dag and plot sheets, CS and RS records, mutation and deed copies), TCB cards and National ID cards are live now. e-Passports and travel documents, and licences and certificates such as driving and trade licences, are rolling out.

items.q: How does it tell a fake from a real card?
items.a: It compares fonts, layout, fine background patterns, microprint, holograms and the MRZ checksum with the genuine template, looks for signs of a photo of a screen or a photocopy, and then matches the card details with the issuing registry before giving a verdict.

items.q: Is the Upokari app available in Bangla?
items.a: Yes. You can switch between Bangla and English anywhere in the app.

items.q: How is my information protected in the app?
items.a: Documents are kept in an encrypted vault with access control, and you can lock the app with Face ID, fingerprint or a PIN.

items.q: Can our organisation send notices or invoices through Upokari?
items.a: Upokari is built as a platform shared by many organisations. Approved organisations connect as senders and deliver digitally signed, QR-coded notices and invoices to people’s wallets. [Contact us](contact:Upokari) to discuss connecting your organisation.
